steps.title: Import React and useId
steps.instruction: Import React and the useId hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useId from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useId hook are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useId are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the useId hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useId from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and the useId hook from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns React's fragment shorthand <> </>.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useId } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named App and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Check the component name and return value.

steps.title: Generate a stable ID with useId
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useId hook and store its return value in a variable named 'id'.
steps.hint: useId is a hook that returns a unique string ID. Call it directly and assign the result to a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: generating an ID
const uniqueId = useId();
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a variable 'id' containing a unique stable identifier generated by useId.
successCriteria: The useId hook is called and its return value is stored in a variable named 'id'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully generated a stable ID using the useId hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useId() and storing the result in a variable named 'id'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useId hook wasn't called correctly. Remember to call useId() and assign its return value to a variable named 'id'.

steps.title: Display the generated ID in the component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the generated ID value. Use the variable you stored the useId result in.
steps.hint: Remember to use JSX curly braces to embed the ID variable inside the paragraph content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a paragraph showing the stable ID generated by useId.
successCriteria: The App component returns a paragraph element containing the ID variable inside JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the stable ID in the UI. This shows how useId generates unique identifiers that persist across renders.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct variable name for the ID and embedding it inside JSX curly braces within a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element isn't displaying the ID correctly. Check that you're using the variable from useId inside JSX curly braces within a

tag.

steps.title: Create a second ID with useId
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call useId again and store the result in a variable named 'secondId'.
steps.hint: You can call useId multiple times in the same component to generate different stable IDs. Add a second call right after the first one.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will now have two stable IDs: 'id' and 'secondId', both generated by useId.
successCriteria: A second call to useId is added, and its result is stored in a variable named 'secondId'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully generated a second stable ID using useId.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useId again and storing the result in a variable named 'secondId'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Try calling useId a second time and storing the result in a variable named 'secondId'.

steps.title: Display the second ID in the component
steps.instruction: Add a second paragraph element that displays the second ID you generated earlier.
steps.hint:
Add another

tag inside the return statement, similar to the first one, but using the 'secondId' variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying a second value

Second value: {secondValue}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display both generated IDs in separate paragraphs.
successCriteria: A second paragraph element exists that displays the value of 'secondId'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a second paragraph to display the second stable ID.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're displaying the 'secondId' variable inside a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to add a paragraph element that shows the second ID.

steps.title: Create a form with label and input
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a <form> element containing a <label> and an <input> field.
steps.hint: The form should be placed within the return statement, typically after any existing elements. Use JSX syntax for the form, label, and input tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a form with a label and an input field, preparing for ID usage in the next steps.
successCriteria: A <form> element containing a <label> and an <input> is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the form structure. This sets up the UI for demonstrating stable IDs with form elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some form elements, but make sure you have both a <label> and an <input> inside the <form>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure isn't complete. Ensure you add a <form> element containing both a <label> and an <input> field.

steps.title: Use the first ID for form accessibility
steps.instruction: Add the htmlFor attribute to the label and the id attribute to the input, both using the first generated ID variable 'id'.
steps.hint: Set htmlFor={id} on the label and id={id} on the input element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The label and input are now connected via the stable ID generated by useId, improving form accessibility.
successCriteria: The label has htmlFor={id} and the input has id={id} using the first useId variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the label and input with the stable ID, making the form accessible.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both the label's htmlFor and the input's id are set to the same ID variable 'id'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The label and input are not properly connected. Check that you're using the 'id' variable from useId for both attributes.

steps.title: Create a second form field with the second ID
steps.instruction: Add a second label and input pair inside the existing form element, using the secondId variable for the htmlFor and id attributes.
steps.hint: Copy the structure of the first label-input pair, but use secondId instead of id for both attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will contain two accessible label-input pairs, each connected with a unique stable ID.
successCriteria: A second label element with htmlFor={secondId}
A second input element with id={secondId}
Both elements are inside the form
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a second accessible form field using the second stable ID.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both the label's htmlFor and input's id attributes use the secondId variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added both a label and input element inside the form, and that they're connected using secondId.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component so it can be imported and used in other files.
steps.hint: Use the export statement you've seen in previous lessons to make the App component available for import elsewhere.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported and ready to be used in other modules.
successCriteria: The App component is exported using export default App.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the App component, making it available for use in other files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct export syntax for the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not exported correctly. Check the export statement syntax.
